verses.text: Job continued his speech:
"As surely as God lives, the God who has denied me justice, the Almighty who has made my life bitter,
as long as I still have breath in me and God's breath is in my nostrils,
my lips will speak no wrong and my tongue will tell no lies.
I'll never say that you are right. I will hold on to my integrity until the day I die.
I hold on to my righteousness and won't let go. My conscience won't accuse me as long as I live.
May my enemy meet the fate of the wicked, and may anyone who rises against me end up like the unjust.
What hope do the godless have when they're cut off, when God takes their life?
Will God hear their cry when trouble overtakes them?
Will they take delight in the Almighty and call on God at all times?
I'll teach you what God's hand can do. I won't hide what the Almighty has in store.
You've all seen it yourselves, so why keep talking nonsense?
This is what God gives the wicked, the inheritance oppressors receive from the Almighty.
No matter how many children they have, the sword waits for them, and their descendants will never have enough bread.
Those who survive them will be carried to their graves, and their widows won't mourn.
They may heap up silver like dust and pile up clothes like dirt.
They may pile it all up, but the righteous will wear the clothes and the innocent will divide the silver.
They build houses as fragile as a moth's shelter, like a temporary hut a watchman sets up.
They lie down rich, but never will again. When they open their eyes, everything is gone.
Terrors overtake them like floodwaters. A storm carries them off in the night.
The east wind lifts them away, and they're gone. It sweeps them out of their home.
It hurls itself at them without pity as they try to escape its grip.
People clap at their downfall and hiss them out of their home."
